newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea mulls more food aid to North Korea. [CORRECTED 04:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: South Korea mulls more food aid to North Korea. [CORRECTED 04:35 GMT]

text.p: South Korea is considering food aid to North Korea by joining urgent international efforts to stave off famine in the impoverished country, a foreign ministry official said on Wednesday.
"We are favourably considering the latest appeal by the World Food Programme to increase aid to North Korea," he said.
The U.N. body last week appealed for $95.5 million (corrects from "an extra $95.5 million") to double its relief food supply to North Korea to 200,000 tonnes from an earlier plan for 100,000 tonnes.
North Korea's food crisis was underscored by news on Tuesday that North Korea had told international aid agencies 134 children had died of malnutrition.
"We have basically decided to increase our contribution to the WFP but we are still discussing the size of the increase," a government official told Reuters.
South Korea has already pledged $6 million to the WFP appeal and the United States $10 million. On Tuesday Washington said it was considering raising its contribution.
